items.title: 如果LLM从未见过超出五年级水平的材料，会怎样？ / What happens when an LLM never sees material beyond fifth grade?

sources.title: 如果LLM从未见过超出五年级水平的材料，会怎样？ / What happens when an LLM never sees material beyond fifth grade?
sources.title_zh: 如果LLM从未见过超出五年级水平的材料，会怎样？
sources.title_en: What happens when an LLM never sees material beyond fifth grade?
sources.title_original: What happens when an LLM never sees material beyond fifth grade?
sources.summary:
Wrong. Quantum entanglement doesn't mean one entangled particle is changing the other one. It means that two particles share a relationship where we intially don't know their state, but if we determine one particle's state we know 100% what's the other particle's state. This has been common and popular misconception long before LLMs. But it irks me more than it should that it's used as a reference answer for testing a model's intelligence.
